stem: Older leaves show deficiency-like discoloration while root-zone EC is already elevated. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Keep the symptom, elevated root-zone EC, pH, irrigation, root-zone moisture, and crop-stage context together before adding fertilizer or assigning a nutrient cause.
Increase fertilizer because older-leaf discoloration plus high root-zone EC means the plant has used up the available nutrients.
Use the elevated EC to identify which specific nutrient is missing from the root zone.
Treat the leaf symptom itself as sufficient confirmation of a deficiency.
rationale: Older-leaf discoloration can be consistent with nutritional stress, but elevated root-zone EC can also reflect concentration, water-balance, pH, availability, or root-function problems. Adding more fertilizer before understanding that context can worsen the condition. Technician I should preserve the symptom and supporting pH/EC/irrigation/root-zone evidence, then escalate interpretation rather than diagnosing from appearance alone.
